newsitem.title: USA: N.J. unemployment rate drops to 5.2 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: N.J. unemployment rate drops to 5.2 pct in April.

text.p: New Jersey's seasonally-adjusted unemployment rate dropped to 5.2 percent in April from 5.5 percent in March, the state's Department of Labor said Friday.
The report marked the fourth straight month of declining unemployment rates for New Jersey since the 6.1 percent figure reported for December.

"This is the lowest rate in the state since August 1990," state Labor Commissioner Mel Gelade said. "At 5.2 percent, New Jersey's April unemployment rate is a full percentage point below last year's average rate and job creation is continuing."
Preliminary figures showed that employment rose by 700 jobs from March, to more than 3.7 million.
Job gains were concentrated in retail trade and eating and drinking establishments, the department said.
Construction employment fell 600, but the department said the drop was due to technical factors and not a decline in construction activity.
Employment in the services sector fell by 900.
